content.text: No liquidated damages, penalties, early-termination fees, late-payment charges or shortfall payments payable by Corio appear anywhere (Sections 4, 9, 11, 13, 17, Exhibit B). Submitting as compliant at the preferred level.

input.quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages or penalties on Corio (our client, the customer/licensee), so it meets the preferred position. Corio's monetary obligations are limited to actual fees for value received: license fees (4.1), annual maintenance and support fees (4.2), taxes (4.3), revenue-sharing and implementation fees (Exhibit B) and standard fees for optional shared resources (13.1-13.2), all payable on the ordinary net-30/acceptance terms in Exhibit B's Payment Terms. Termination (11.1-11.2) is by non-renewal notice or for uncured material breach or insolvency, with no early-termination fee, minimum-fee shortfall, acceleration of remaining contract value or forfeiture on termination; post-termination payments under 11.3 are only continuing support/maintenance fees for services Corio elects to keep receiving. Section 9 further caps each party's liability at amounts actually paid by Corio, reinforcing that no stipulated or penal sum runs against us. The only true-up mechanics are the audit provisions in 4.4 (payment of an actual shortfall and reimbursement of examination cost on a >5% underpayment), which are compensatory audit terms rather than liquidated damages, and we note them for information only. No fallback early-termination-fee cap is needed because no Customer-payable liquidated amount exists.
